title: Some moments have an expiration date
core_truth: Not everything unfinished deserves more of my attention than something meaningful with an expiration date.
story_evidence: Mario felt anxious about unfinished work and responsibilities while choosing to spend an ordinary day with Kelly before she left. They ran errands, had lunch, and laughed for hours. He concluded that the tasks could wait but that particular day could not be recreated.

title: What stays hidden becomes insecurity
core_truth: Unspoken fear compounds. Honest conversation interrupts it before it turns into anxiety, insecurity, or jealousy.
story_evidence: Mario wrote out and named comparison wounds that surfaced in a conversation about past partners, then discussed them directly instead of allowing them to become anxiety or jealousy. The conversation created relief and intimacy.

title: You'll Never Be Ready
core_truth: Readiness is not a feeling. It is a decision.
story_evidence: Mario states that he was not ready to move to Mexico, start over, or leave everything he had built behind. He did it anyway while scared and uncertain.

title: The Shit Nobody Tells You About Starting Over
core_truth: You cannot become someone new while protecting someone you used to be.
story_evidence: Mario states that he spent years building one life and then lost it. For a while he treated that loss as the end of his story before reframing it as the old identity's expiration date.

title: Rebuilding in Public
core_truth: An unfinished reinvention is worth documenting without pretending it is already a success story.
story_evidence: Mario states that he moved countries, questioned everything, and began rebuilding from a place he never expected to be. He chose to document the doubt, work, mistakes, and small wins before knowing how the story ends.

title: The Hardest Part Isn't Money
core_truth: The hardest loss is often the identity attached to what disappeared, not the thing itself.
story_evidence: Mario states that after losing the life he had built, he was grieving the identity of business owner, successful person, and the guy who had it figured out more than the money itself.

title: Bring Back Not Giving a Fuck
core_truth: Trading your future for other people's temporary opinions is too expensive.
story_evidence: Mario states that when he moved to Mexico after his life fell apart, people talked. He moved anyway and describes the move as another chance at life.

title: Shit I Wish Someone Told Me Earlier
core_truth: Confidence and standards are built through action, discomfort, and lessons learned the expensive way.
story_evidence: Mario states that he learned these lessons by ignoring them first, including that confidence follows surviving hard things, relief is not peace, and tolerated behavior becomes a standard.

title: Self-Improvement Advice That Can Fuck Off
core_truth: Advice that only makes you feel better is not always advice that makes you better.
story_evidence: Mario's existing production piece rejects passive slogans about fate, peace, authenticity, process, and timing in favor of responsibility, useful conflict, change, and action.

title: Stop Looking for a Sign
core_truth: The right time rarely arrives; taking one real step ends the lie that you are still deciding.
story_evidence: Mario states that he spent years waiting for business stability, money, confidence, and clarity until everything fell apart anyway. He now treats an irreversible first step as the end of indecision.

title: Your Comfort Zone Is a Manipulative Little Bitch
core_truth: Recovery should prepare you to move again, not become a permanent address.
story_evidence: Mario states that comfort almost convinced him not to move or rebuild. Moving allowed him to meet a version of himself he would not have reached by staying predictable.

title: I Turned Failure Into an Identity
core_truth: You can own what happened without becoming what happened.
story_evidence: Mario states that after things went wrong, he began describing himself through failure. He distinguishes failing at an event from adopting failure as an identity that lowers future standards and effort.
